headline: A REAL BROWSER NOW EXECUTES THE DEPLOYED BYTES. Chromium cannot TLS-handshake through this container's egress proxy — that is measured, not assumed, and the cause is narrowed to ALPN h2 on the tunnel. Node's TLS does traverse it, so tools/playability/live-mirror.mjs fetches the live site over the proxy and re-serves it on 127.0.0.1 at the owner's own path shape. It is not 'Chromium spoke to github.io' and the tool says so. Separately: the blog page on the live site embeds twelve images that 404, and the instrument that was supposed to guarantee playability had a latch that could zero its own number on a game drawing perfectly.

constraint_item_1.question: can a browser in this container reach github.io?
constraint_item_1.answer: NO, and the reason is now known rather than guessed.
evidence: raw CONNECT from python to 127.0.0.1:38351 -> 'HTTP/1.1 200 Connection Established'. The tunnel is fine.
curl through the same proxy: 200, 517-byte ClientHello, ALPN h2 accepted, real *.github.io cert.

chromium --proxy-server=http://127.0.0.1:38351: CONNECT accepted (200), then upstream ECONNRESET after a 1768-byte ClientHello. Same for example.com and raw.githubusercontent.com, so it is CHROMIUM'S HANDSHAKE and not the destination.

tried and did not help: --disable-features=PostQuantumKyber,UseMLKEM,EncryptedClientHello; --disable-quic; --disable-http2; --ssl-version-max=tls1.2. Measured ClientHello stayed 1736-1832 bytes in all six variants.

NARROWED: node's own TLS through the tunnel succeeds with default ALPN, and FAILS with ECONNRESET the moment ALPNProtocols ['h2','http/1.1'] is offered. That is chromium's default and is very likely the whole cause.

ALSO FOUND: an https.Agent with keepAlive over pooled tunnels makes the proxy answer 403 x-deny-reason:host_not_allowed for a host the same process fetches 200 with `Connection: close`. Isolated four ways. The mirror therefore uses one tunnel per request and is slower on purpose.
what_i_could_not_test: the CDN's own TLS as a browser sees it
HTTP/2 multiplexing and Pages' real cache headers (the mirror serves 1.1 and no-store, i.e. always a cold load)
a real phone. Every reading here is desktop Chromium wearing a phone's viewport, dpr, UA and touch. That is stated everywhere it matters and it is the standing limit of this role.

defects_found.what: twelve images the blog embeds 404 for every visitor: ../reports/wld12-blind/f12.png through f22.png. The files exist on disk and are UNTRACKED (git ls-files reports/wld12-blind/ is empty), so they were never published. The owner reading the blog sees twelve broken images.
defects_found.owner: not mine — reports/ and the blog generator belong elsewhere. Reported, not fixed.

defects_found.what: READ LATCH. Its readPixels probe called canvas.getContext() at 15 s. A canvas has one context: if the probe wins the race the renderer inherits a context with preserveDrawingBuffer:false and every readPixels returns zero FOREVER on a game that is drawing perfectly. Found by the W1-DEPLOY r1 critic; fixed here by refusing to read until window.__ENGINE.renderer exists.

Its four viewports rendered one identical 1920x1080 framebuffer, because main.js takes the automation branch when navigator.webdriver is true and skips the resize. A four-device check was a one-device check wearing four hats. Fixed: webdriver is spoofed false, AND the tool now fails a row whose framebuffer is not this device's shape — 1920x1080 is the literal in the <canvas> tag, i.e. the value you get when nothing ever resized it.

THE DIAGNOSTIC COULD NOT BE COPIED. body sets user-select:none and -webkit-touch-callout:none, which the game needs and #boot-notice inherited. The notice says 'Please send this line' under a <code> block that on a phone cannot be selected. The one artefact it exists to deliver could not be delivered.
defects_found.fix: one-tap copy button with a selection fallback, and user-select:text on the code block

defects_found.what: deviceLine() was attached to exactly two failure paths — context-lost and booted-but-blank. The two failures that actually reached the owner (a 404'd module, a thrown error) printed nothing about the browser at all. Now say(bad=true) appends it on every path.

deviceLine() wrapped every probe in ONE try, and `gl instanceof WebGL2RenderingContext` throws ReferenceError on a browser with no WebGL2 constructor — an old phone, which is the only hardware the line is written for. It would have printed the canvas size and then stopped. Now every fact is probed independently.

deviceLine() called getContext on the GAME's canvas. Harmless while it only ran after boot; the moment it runs on an early failure (P5) it becomes the same latch as P2, shipped into the game. Now every LIMIT is asked of a throwaway canvas (limits are device properties, not canvas properties) and only attrs/isContextLost/getError read the real context, and only once __ENGINE.renderer exists.
reported a picture that is demonstrably there as broken, on a transient 503 from Pages' CDN under a 100-path sweep. Now retries 5xx twice with backoff and never retries a 404.

capabilities_added_to_the_boot_notice: navigator.deviceMemory and hardwareConcurrency — a 17 MB world dying of memory pressure is the likeliest phone refusal and neither number appears in any desktop failure
MAX_VARYING_VECTORS and MAX_VERTEX_TEXTURE_IMAGE_UNITS — limits that break a shader silently rather than throwing, so they never reach the error handler
float-renderable colour buffer (EXT/WEBGL_color_buffer_float) — the classic older-iOS refusal; a renderer wanting one gets an incomplete framebuffer and draws black
the context attributes the renderer ACTUALLY got (antialias/depth/preserveDrawingBuffer), which under memory pressure is not what it asked for
the build commit and pathname — without it a report is about 'the game', and the game changes several times an hour

defect_P12.where: tools/world/verify-playable.mjs — a coupling that commit a52113c would have broken silently
defect_P12.what: the pixel reading was gl.readPixels on the game's own canvas, which only works while the renderer sets preserveDrawingBuffer. a52113c turned that off for players — correctly, a second full-size buffer with antialias is a known way to lose a phone's GL context — and this tool runs as a PERSON on purpose (webdriver spoofed false, so main.js takes the real resize path). From that commit onward it would have read all-zero from a game drawing perfectly and reported a black screen forever.
defect_P12.fix: two layers. First a guard: it asks getContextAttributes and, if the buffer is not preserved, reports UNMEASURED with the reason instead of reporting black — a silent false negative turned into a loud one. Then the real fix: the measurement now comes from a SCREENSHOT, drawn into a 2-D canvas in the page and reduced on the same grid. That is the composited page, which is what the question was always about, it includes HTML overlays like the boot notice, nothing inside the page can flatter it, and it has no relationship to the WebGL context at all. The GL read remains as a fallback and the run says which it used.
defect_P12.caught_by: watching a neighbour's commit go past in `pgrep -a git` while waiting for the index lock. It was not caught by any check.

defect_P10_THE_IMPORTANT_ONE.what: THE GAME'S DATA LOADER HAS NO RETRY. `const res = await fetch(...); if (!res.ok) throw new Error('data file missing: ' + rel + ' (' + res.status + ')')`. Any non-200 on any of several hundred data files kills the entire boot, and the boot notice then tells the player 'A file the game needs is missing.' — which is wrong, because nothing is missing.
defect_P10_THE_IMPORTANT_ONE.how_i_found_it: not by reading the code. Two live runs died at `data file missing: world/hazards.json (503)`. Pages' CDN answered 503 under my sweep, the file is there, and the game gave up on it. That is the failure arriving by itself, on the real host, which is the only reason anyone would believe it.
defect_P10_THE_IMPORTANT_ONE.why_it_matters: this is a black screen that a phone on a flaky connection can produce and this build machine essentially never will, because a local static server does not drop requests. It is a live candidate explanation for the owner's black screen that costs nothing to rule out and that no check in this project could previously have seen. It is also the exact shape of failure the README currently describes as 'It is not the controls and it is not a missing file. Every check passes on the build machine.'
defect_P10_THE_IMPORTANT_ONE.owner: NOT MINE — game/src/engine.js belongs to the engine pieces. Reported, not fixed, per file ownership.
defect_P10_THE_IMPORTANT_ONE.recommended_fix: retry a non-ok fetch two or three times with a short backoff before throwing, and distinguish 404 (genuinely missing — do not retry, the message is right) from 5xx and network errors (transient — retry, and if it still fails say 'the connection dropped' rather than 'a file is missing'). Roughly six lines.
defect_P10_THE_IMPORTANT_ONE.reproduce: node tools/world/verify-playable.mjs --cap-ms 480000 — the run reports how many times the live host 5xx'd, and the mirror retries where the game does not.

defect_P13_LIVE_RIGHT_NOW.severity: the boot notice is a full-screen RED ERROR over a working game, on the deployed bytes, right now
defect_P13_LIVE_RIGHT_NOW.what: painted() decides whether the game has drawn by calling gl.readPixels on the GAME'S OWN drawing buffer, from a setInterval. Commit a52113c set preserveDrawingBuffer:false for anyone who is not automated - correctly, it is a known way to lose a phone's context. After compositing, a non-preserved drawing buffer is specified to be undefined and is zero in practice. So for EVERY REAL PLAYER painted() returns false on a game drawing perfectly, forever.
defect_P13_LIVE_RIGHT_NOW.consequence: the notice's poll then runs: at sinceBoot > 6 s it calls say('The world loaded, but nothing is being drawn.', ..., bad=true) - the RED state, with the copy button and the device line - and only at sinceBoot > 20 s does the ceiling hide it. #boot-notice is position:fixed; inset:0; z-index:9999 with NO pointer-events:none, so for those ~14 seconds it covers the whole screen, eats every tap and click, and tells the player the game is broken while the game is running underneath it.
defect_P13_LIVE_RIGHT_NOW.why_nothing_caught_it: this is the SAME defect class as the corner-sampled painted() the W1-DEPLOY critic found, arriving by a different route, and it lives in a window every instrument stops short of. verify-playable's last sample is ~3-4 s after boot; the notice's own timer needs 6 s. Rule 8 in the small: the check measured the one interval at which its number is zero. The predecessor moved THE INSTRUMENT to a screenshot for exactly this coupling and left THE SHIPPED PAGE reading readPixels.
defect_P13_LIVE_RIGHT_NOW.on_the_live_site: YES. curl of the deployed game/index.html has the readPixels painted() at line 229 and the deployed game/src/render/renderer.js has `preserveDrawingBuffer: automated` at line 59. Both halves are published.

defect_P13_LIVE_RIGHT_NOW.fix: painted() must not read the GL buffer. Either read a 2-D canvas copy of the composited page, or - cheaper and with no pixel read at all - treat 'the renderer exists and its frame counter has advanced since the last poll' as painted, which is what the notice actually wants to know.

P13_fix.where: game/index.html — painted(), and the poll's clock
three_changes: THE READ MOVED INSIDE requestAnimationFrame. That is the whole fix and it is the thing the three-way measurement above decided: the same frame reads 0/2880 from a timer and 2753/2880 inside a frame.

THE READ BECAME RARE. One in flight, at most one every 2 s, and it stops the moment the answer is yes. Fewer pixels was NOT the saving — 16 band reads cost as much as 2,280 single-pixel reads — so the count had to come down, not the area.

IT NO LONGER ACCUSES ON A READ IT COULD NOT GET. If the pixels are unreadable but the renderer's own frame counter is advancing and it is issuing draw calls, painted() returns true and the notice hides. Saying 'nothing is being drawn' when you have failed to look is how this defect happened twice; the notice may only say it when it has actually seen black. window.__BOOT_PAINT_EVIDENCE records which of the two signals decided each run, so nobody has to guess.
P13_fix.fourth_change_separate_defect: the poll's `sinceBoot` was `+= 0.2` per 200 ms tick, i.e. a count of ticks pretending to be seconds. With painted() costing 8.8 s a call the ticks were nowhere near 200 ms apart, so the twenty-second escape hatch was over a minute of wall clock. It is Date.now() now. A rescue timer that runs slow exactly when the page is in trouble is the wrong clock.
P13_fix.what_is_NOT_changed: game/src/render/renderer.js. a52113c is right — preserveDrawingBuffer off for players is a real protection for a phone's GL context, and the diagnostic must adapt to it rather than the other way round.
